name: Native Email (SMTP / Transactional API) & Telegram Bot Notification Integrations
target_personas: PER-01;PER-02;PER-05;PER-07;PER-03
plain_language_summary: Delivers two essential, zero-middleware outbound notification channels out of the box: (1) **Native Email** via standard `SMTP` / `STARTTLS` / `SMTPS` (compatible with corporate Postfix/Exchange air-gap relays, Gmail, Microsoft 365, and Amazon SES / Resend / Postmark transactional APIs) with clean 15-language HTML + plaintext templates; and (2) **First-Class Telegram Bot Integration** (Vault-sealed bot token, chat ID & supergroup forum `message_thread_id` support, severity filters, and 1-click interactive test ping).
practical_example:
**Self-Hosted (`PER-01`):** Maya pastes her `@BotFather` token (sealed in Vault) and personal `chat_id` into `Settings -> Notifications -> Telegram`, clicks `Send Test Message`, and immediately gets a crisp mobile push alert whenever her USD 50 monthly OpenAI/Anthropic budget hits `80%` or `100%`.
**Enterprise (`PER-05`, `PER-07`):** An enterprise connects its internal `smtp-relay.corp.internal:587` (`STARTTLS` + custom internal Root CA) to deliver 15-locale user onboarding invitations, Four-Eyes approval emails, weekly executive FinOps spend digests, and `TANPOPO-SA-*` security advisories.
key_trade_offs: Inbound interactive Telegram button callbacks require either a public webhook URL or an outbound long-poll loop (undesirable in strict egress firewalls); therefore, v1 Telegram integration is **strictly outbound push + deep link to the Console** (`0` inbound ports or background polling required), while optional authenticated callbacks are deferred (`[DESIGN_PROPOSAL]`).
user_problem_and_business_value: Eliminates forcing solo users (`PER-01`) to deploy external webhook-to-Telegram Python scripts just to watch homelab spend, and unblocks essential enterprise email workflows (member invitations `FEAT-066`, password reset `FEAT-060`, scheduled FinOps reports `FEAT-041`, and compliance alerts) without external SaaS lock-in.
existing_rc9_behavior_and_limitations: `MISSING` (`[SOURCE_VERIFIED]`): Frozen RC9 has **zero `SMTP` / email sender and zero Telegram Bot integration**; member onboarding and password resets have no email transport, and alerts can only emit raw JSON HTTP webhooks.
proposed_functional_behavior:
1. **Native Email (`SMTP` & Transactional HTTP Adapters):**
   - Supports `SMTP` (`25`/`587` `STARTTLS` with mandatory TLS minimum `1.2`, `465` implicit TLS, `PLAIN` / `LOGIN` / `CRAM-MD5` / `XOAUTH2`, custom corporate Root CA bundle, and explicit internal-relay CIDR allowlist for air-gapped Postfix/Exchange servers) plus HTTPS transactional adapters (`AWS SES v2` via `SigV4`, `Microsoft Graph Mail`, `Resend` / `SendGrid`).
   - Ships 15-locale offline-bundled responsive **Multipart `text/plain` + Astryx-styled `text/html`** templates (strictly `0` external tracking pixels, `0` remote webfont/image links!) covering: Workspace Invitations, Password Reset / MFA Recovery notices, Four-Eyes & MCP Approval Requests, Budget Threshold & Burn-Rate Alerts, Scheduled Daily/Weekly FinOps Digests, Expiring Credentials, and Security Quarantine / `TANPOPO-SA-*` Advisories.
   - Enforces header-injection sanitization (`CR`/`LF` stripping on `Subject`/`To`/`From` display names) and optional `S/MIME` or `DKIM`-friendly canonical headers.
2. **First-Class Telegram Bot Channel:**
   - Seals Bot Token in Vault (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` — write-only, never returned to UI after save); supports private `chat_id`, group/channel IDs, and Telegram Supergroup Forum **`message_thread_id` (Topics)** so teams can route `#security` vs `#finops` into separate topics of one group.
   - Formats MarkdownV2-escaped structured cards (`Severity`, `Org/Project`, `Event`, `Metric/Spend`, `Timestamp`, and Console Deep Link) via `SSRFGuard`-pinned `api.telegram.org` (or custom self-hosted `telegram-bot-api` base URL) with `429 retry_after` rate-limit compliance and 1-click `Send Test Message`.
user_facing_subfeatures: Console `Email (SMTP / API)` setup drawer with TLS/STARTTLS verifier, internal-relay CIDR consent, and `Send Test Email` button. | 15-Language Offline HTML + Plaintext Email Template Previewer (`SCR-16` / `/settings/notifications`). | Console `Telegram Bot` channel card with Vault-sealed Bot Token, `chat_id` + Forum Topic (`message_thread_id`) fields, severity filter, and `Send Test Message`. | Delivery telemetry (`Sent`, `Retrying`, `Bounced/Failed`, `429 Rate-Limited`) integrated into the unified Delivery Inspector (`FEAT-114`).
end_to_end_lifecycle: Admin selects SMTP or Telegram template (`FEAT-116`), seals credential in Vault, clicks `Test Connection` -> enables channel in Org/Personal Routing Matrix (`FEAT-112`) -> `ARCH-016` async outbox formats localized payload & dispatches with exponential backoff -> delivery receipt logged in `notification_deliveries`.
primary_and_alternative_journeys:
**Primary (Homelab Telegram Setup in `< 60s` `[HYPOTHESIS]`):** User creates bot via `@BotFather`, pastes token + chat ID, clicks `Send Test Message`, and enables `Budget >= 80%` + `Security Critical` alerts.
**Alternative (Air-Gapped Corporate SMTP Relay):** Operator points Tanpopo at `10.10.4.25:587` (`STARTTLS`) with internal CA cert; invitations and Four-Eyes alerts flow across internal corporate mail with `0` internet egress.
admin_and_permission_boundaries: Instance-wide SMTP transport (`invitations`, `password_reset`, `SYSTEM` alerts) is configured by `OPERATOR`; org-specific custom SMTP overrides and org/project Telegram Bot sinks are configurable by `ORG_OWNER` / `TEAM_ADMIN` (subject to org egress allowlists).
automation_opportunities: Scheduled Weekly/Monthly FinOps Executive Summary emails (`FEAT-041` + `FEAT-112`) and automated credential-rotation reminder emails before `vk_tp_*`, `sak_tp_*`, or `SAML` certs expire.
enterprise_requirements: Zero external tracking pixels or CDN assets inside HTML emails, strict CRLF header-injection defense, per-recipient rate-limiting (preventing password-reset/invite email bombing), and `BlindHostCredentialBroker` / Vault token custody so bot tokens and SMTP passwords never appear in logs or support bundles.
touchpoint_console: `Settings -> Notifications & Channels` Email (`SMTP`/SES/Graph) & Telegram Bot configuration drawers + template preview.
touchpoint_gitops: Declarative `notificationChannels[]` referencing `${VAULT:<smtp_or_telegram_slot>}` (`0` plaintext secrets in Git).
dependencies_and_relationships: Integrates with `FEAT-112` (Notification Center & Routing Matrix), `FEAT-116` (Turnkey Setup Templates), `ARCH-016` (Async Outbox), `FEAT-059` (Vault), and `ARCH-009` (`SSRFGuard`).;Unlocks email delivery for `FEAT-060` (password reset) and `FEAT-066` (member invitations).
failure_and_recovery_behavior: Transient `SMTP 4xx` or Telegram `HTTP 429` (`parameters.retry_after`) responses reschedule automatically in the `ARCH-016` outbox with jittered backoff; permanent `5xx` auth/chat failures surface a clear `Channel Degraded` banner in `FEAT-112` In-App Inbox and retain events in the Dead-Letter Queue (`FEAT-114`) for replay after credential fix.
security_privacy_and_financial_implicati: Enforces `STARTTLS` certificate verification by default (forbidding opportunistic cleartext downgrade when `tls_mode = REQUIRE_STARTTLS`), redacts email addresses/chat IDs in `SYSTEM` support bundles, and includes `0` raw prompt payloads in outbound messages.
preliminary_acceptance_criteria: Hermetic E2E test against local `Mailpit`/`GreenMail` (`STARTTLS`) and mock `Telegram Bot API` verifies 15-locale multipart email rendering (`0` external URLs, `0` CRLF header injection) and MarkdownV2-escaped Telegram forum-topic delivery. | Bot tokens and SMTP passwords are stored write-only in Vault (`GET /notification-channels` returns masked slot metadata only). | Telegram `429 retry_after` response pauses channel dispatch for the specified duration and delivers queued alerts without loss.
evidence_and_confidence: `HIGH` — `[SOURCE_VERIFIED]` absence of SMTP & Telegram in RC9 (`TEEP-01-DOC-04`); standard RFC 5321/3207 pure-Go `net/smtp` + `crypto/tls` (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) and Telegram Bot HTTPS JSON API.
priority_rationale: P1-Enterprise-Core because **Email (`SMTP`)** is universal across every enterprise (`PER-05`, `PER-07`) for workspace invitations, local password resets, Four-Eyes approvals, and FinOps digests (including internal air-gap Postfix/Exchange relays), while **Telegram Bot** is the #1 beloved zero-cost mobile push channel among homelab and indie self-hosters (`PER-01`, `PER-02`) who do not run PagerDuty or Enterprise Slack.
placement_rationale: Pure-Go `SMTP`/`STARTTLS` delivery (needed for core IAM user invitations & local break-glass password reset flows) and native Telegram Bot `NOTIFICATION_SINK` ship built-in with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, backed by Vault secret sealing and `SSRFGuard`.

name: Signed Outbound Event Webhooks, Delivery History Inspector & Dead-Letter Replay
target_personas: PER-03;PER-04;PER-05;PER-07
plain_language_summary: Hardens and completes Tanpopo's signed outbound webhooks: decouples global quarantine fan-out into an `O(k_affected)` asynchronous outbox worker (`ARCH-016`, `FND-009`), restores `ORG_OWNER` self-service access, unlocks full URL/event/secret editing + dual-secret zero-downtime rotation, expands the event taxonomy across all platform domains, and adds a **Delivery History & Dead-Letter Queue (`DLQ`) Inspector** with 1-click test-ping and replay.
practical_example: A tenant `ORG_OWNER` (`PER-04`) opens `/settings/webhooks`, edits an automation endpoint URL, sends a `Test Ping` (verifying `200 OK` in `142 ms` and `X-Tanpopo-Signature-256`), and later inspects 3 failed `502 Bad Gateway` attempts in the `Dead-Letter Queue` after an internal receiver outage — clicking `Replay Failed Deliveries` to redeliver the exact signed `budget.burn_anomaly` events with original `event_id` idempotency keys.
key_trade_offs: Storing per-attempt HTTP status, latency, and sanitized error headers in `webhook_deliveries` increases OLTP write volume if unbounded; Tanpopo caps stored response snippets to `<= 512 B` (headers/status redacted of `Set-Cookie`/tokens) and reaps delivery logs via `ttl.Cleaner` (`FEAT-051`, `default 14d`).
user_problem_and_business_value: Eliminates blind webhook debugging when downstream receivers rotate secrets or return `500`s, restores tenant `ORG_OWNER` autonomy (`FND-009`), and prevents global extension quarantines from stalling behind `2 * N_orgs` synchronous outbox loops (`ARCH-OBS-01`).
existing_rc9_behavior_and_limitations: `PARTIAL_IMPLEMENTATION` with verified defects (`[SOURCE_VERIFIED]`, `FND-009`, `ARCH-OBS-01`): (1) `cmd/tanpopo/serve.go:1046` invokes `O(N_orgs)` outbox insertion **twice synchronously** during global extension quarantine; (2) `webhook_event_outbox` lacks a partial PG index `(org_id) WHERE dispatched_at_ms IS NULL` (`FND-002`); (3) `OperationsPage.tsx` bundles `/settings/webhooks` with retention settings under `OPERATOR`-only gating, locking out `ORG_OWNER`s! (4) `OperationsPage.tsx:207` only toggles `{enabled}` (cannot edit `target_url`, `events`, or rotate `secret`); (5) zero `webhook_deliveries` API/UI, test-ping, or DLQ replay exists; and (6) only `4` event types exist.
proposed_functional_behavior:
1. Outbox Scalability & RBAC Decoupling (`CAP-125`, `ARCH-016`, `FND-009`): Move global quarantine fan-out to an async `SYSTEM` job querying only `O(k_affected)` orgs (`ARCH-011`) with `1` idempotent insert per org; add PG partial index `idx_webhook_outbox_pending (org_id, next_attempt_at_ms) WHERE dispatched_at_ms IS NULL`; and move Webhooks to a dedicated `ORG_OWNER`-accessible `/settings/webhooks` route.
2. Full Subscription Lifecycle & Dual-Secret Rotation (`CAP-126`): `PATCH /webhooks/{id}` for `target_url`, `events`, custom headers (Vault-sealed), `enabled`, and dual-active signing secret rotation (`v1=<hmac>,v2=<hmac>` during configurable grace window).
3. Expanded `30+` Event Taxonomy (`CloudEvents 1.0` compatible envelope): `budget.{threshold,exhausted,burn_anomaly,rollover}`, `model.{deprecated,migrated}`, `mcp.{schema_drift,hitl_requested,hitl_resolved}`, `four_eyes.{requested,approved,rejected}`, `security.{killswitch_triggered,extension_quarantined,advisory_matched}`, `iam.{scim_deprovisioned,key_expiring}`, `policy.what_if_completed`.
4. Delivery History, `Test Ping` & `DLQ Replay`: Inspect per-attempt timestamp, HTTP status, `duration_ms`, and retry schedule (`8` exponential retries -> `DEAD_LETTER`); 1-click `Send Test Event` and single/bulk `Replay`.
user_facing_subfeatures: Dedicated `/settings/webhooks` page accessible to `ORG_OWNER` (`FND-009`) with full Create / Edit / Dual-Secret Rotate / Disable / Delete. | Expanded `30+` domain event selector grouped by Security, FinOps, Governance, Models, MCP/A2A, and Operations. | Per-Subscription `Delivery History` & `Dead-Letter Queue` drawer showing HTTP status codes, attempt timings, and sanitized error diagnostics. | Rate-limited `Send Test Ping` button and single/bulk `Replay Dead-Letter Events` action.
end_to_end_lifecycle: Create subscription (sealing `HMAC` secret in Vault) -> `Send Test Ping` verifies `2xx` -> domain TX writes idempotent `webhook_event_outbox` row -> `ARCH-016` worker signs `t=<ts>,v1=<hmac>` over canonical JSON & delivers via `SSRFGuard` -> `2xx` marks `DELIVERED` or `8` failures move to `DEAD_LETTER` (triggering `FEAT-112` in-app alert) -> operator fixes endpoint & clicks `Replay`.
primary_and_alternative_journeys:
**Primary (Tenant Self-Service):** `ORG_OWNER` configures a webhook for `budget.burn_anomaly` and `mcp.schema_drift`, rotates the HMAC signing secret zero-downtime with a `24h` dual-signature window, and monitors `99.9%` delivery success.
**Alternative (DLQ Incident Recovery):** Downstream receiver cert expires over a weekend; Monday morning admin renews cert and bulk-replays `18` `DEAD_LETTER` events with original `idempotency_key`s.
admin_and_permission_boundaries: `ORG_OWNER` manages org-scoped webhooks (`FORCE RLS` isolated); `TEAM_ADMIN` can optionally manage project-filtered webhooks if permitted by org policy; `OPERATOR` manages `SYSTEM`-scope operational webhooks.
automation_opportunities: Auto-pause (`CIRCUIT_OPEN`) noisy failing endpoints after `N` consecutive `DEAD_LETTER` exhaustions with an automatic In-App/Email alert (`FEAT-112`/`113`) so dead receivers do not waste worker sockets.
enterprise_requirements: Least-privileged `tanpopo_webhook_worker` PostgreSQL role preserved, `HTTPS`-only enforcement in production with connect-time `SSRFGuard` IP pinning (`ARCH-009`), and live PostgreSQL subscriber `HMAC` E2E verification (`FND-018`).
touchpoint_console: `/settings/webhooks` CRUD, Event Taxonomy Picker, `Test Ping` modal, and `Deliveries / DLQ` inspector drawer.
touchpoint_gitops: Declarative `webhooks[]` resources in `tanpopo config` and Terraform `tanpopo_webhook`.
dependencies_and_relationships: Consolidates `CAP-125` & `CAP-126`; resolves `FND-009` (`ARCH-016` + `FND-002` index #5 + `ORG_OWNER` UI fix) and RC9 PG webhook E2E item (`FND-018`).;Underpins `FEAT-115` (`NOTIFICATION_SINK` ChatOps connectors).
failure_and_recovery_behavior: Transactional outbox guarantees at-least-once queueing committed atomically with the originating business event; worker crashes recover un-dispatched rows cleanly after lease timeout using immutable `event_id` headers for downstream receiver deduplication.
security_privacy_and_financial_implicati: Timestamped `X-Tanpopo-Signature-256` (`t=...,v1=...`) prevents replay attacks; response body logging strips any reflected auth headers and truncates at `512 B` to prevent log-injection / secret reflection.
preliminary_acceptance_criteria: `ORG_OWNER` (`non-OPERATOR`) can create, edit, test-ping, inspect deliveries, rotate secret, replay DLQ, and delete org webhooks in Web Console (`FND-009` closed). | Global extension quarantine inserts at most `1` outbox event per affected org asynchronously (`0` duplicate rows, `O(k_affected)` queries) and passes live PostgreSQL HMAC subscriber verification. | `SSRFGuard` blocks webhook targets resolving to loopback/link-local/`169.254.169.254` (including DNS rebinding and `302` redirects) and records rejection telemetry (`FND-016`).
evidence_and_confidence: `HIGH` — `[SOURCE_VERIFIED]` inspection of `serve.go:1046`, `OperationsPage.tsx:207`, and `0001_full_schema_rls_partitions.sql` (`TEEP-01-DOC-04`, `12`).
priority_rationale: P1-Enterprise-Core because RC9's webhook subsystem suffers three concrete defects (`FND-009` — synchronous duplicate `O(N_orgs)` quarantine fan-out, missing pending outbox PG index, and `ORG_OWNER` RBAC lockout in UI) plus severe Day-2 blind spots (create-only URLs, `4` events only, zero delivery status logs, and zero DLQ replay).
placement_rationale: Transactional outbox durability (`ARCH-016`), `HMAC-SHA256` timestamped payload signing, `SSRFGuard` egress pinning, and tenant-isolated `webhook_deliveries` inspection are core Control-Plane reliability primitives.

subdomain: ChatOps, Incident Paging & Verified HITL Callbacks
name: ChatOps & Incident-Response Connectors (Slack, Teams, Discord, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Jira, ServiceNow) with HITL Callbacks
target_personas: PER-03;PER-05;PER-08;PER-04
plain_language_summary: Provides signed, turnkey connectors formatting Tanpopo alerts and approvals natively for **Slack (`Block Kit`)**, **Microsoft Teams (`Adaptive Cards`)**, **Discord**, **PagerDuty (`Events API v2` with auto-resolve `dedup_key`)**, **Opsgenie**, **Jira / Linear** issue creation, and **ServiceNow** incidents — including cryptographically verified interactive **Human-in-the-Loop (`HITL`) approval callbacks** for `SM-06` MCP tools and Four-Eyes changes.
practical_example: When an autonomous coding agent invokes a mutating `prod_db__execute_migration` MCP tool (`SM-06` HITL hold), Slack `#ai-approvals` receives a formatted Block Kit card showing tool arguments JCS digest, requester, and `Approve` / `Deny` buttons. Clicking `Approve` verifies Slack's HMAC signature **and** requires an authenticated Tanpopo OIDC/SSO session binding + 5-tuple JCS hash match (`0` trust in spoofable chat display names!), unblocking the waiting agent stream in seconds (`[HYPOTHESIS]`).
key_trade_offs: Direct one-click chat approval without SSO binding is insecure if a Slack workspace has guest users or shared channels; enforcing authenticated Tanpopo OIDC principal binding (cached SSO browser step-up or linked verified identity) adds a 1-time account link or quick OIDC click in exchange for non-repudiable Four-Eyes / `SM-06` auditability.
user_problem_and_business_value: Eliminates bespoke webhook-translator microservices across every enterprise adopter, auto-resolves PagerDuty incidents when circuit breakers or Data-Plane quorum recover, and cuts mean-time-to-approve (`MTTA`) on `SM-06` MCP tool holds and Four-Eyes change requests from hours to seconds (`[HYPOTHESIS]`).
existing_rc9_behavior_and_limitations: `MISSING` (`[SOURCE_VERIFIED]`): Frozen RC9 emits generic JSON webhook payloads only; zero native formatters for Slack, Teams, Discord, PagerDuty, Jira, or ServiceNow exist, and approvals require manual Console polling.
proposed_functional_behavior:
1. Signed First-Party `NOTIFICATION_SINK` Connectors (`@tanpopo/notify-{slack,teams,discord,pagerduty,opsgenie,jira,servicenow}`):
   - **ChatOps (`Slack`, `MS Teams`, `Discord`):** Rich native cards (`Block Kit`, `Adaptive Cards v1.5`, Discord embeds) with severity styling, `tabular-nums` spend/latency metrics, thread grouping, and deep links.
   - **On-Call Paging (`PagerDuty Events v2`, `Opsgenie`):** Bidirectional `trigger` -> `acknowledge` -> `resolve` lifecycle keyed by deterministic `dedup_key` so recovering circuit breakers or Valkey clusters automatically resolve open pages!
   - **ITSM Ticketing (`Jira`, `Linear`, `ServiceNow`):** Creates/updates structured compliance, model-deprecation (`FEAT-022`), or security-advisory (`FEAT-150`) tickets with idempotent external issue keys.
2. Zero-Trust Interactive `HITL` Callback Verification (`SM-06` & `Four-Eyes`):
   - Verifies platform request signature + replay window (`<= 5m` `X-Slack-Request-Timestamp` / Teams JWT) **plus** requires verified Tanpopo principal identity (`OIDC`/`SAML` step-up or cryptographically bound principal mapping), enforces self-approval prohibition (`requester != approver`), and validates the exact 5-tuple JCS payload hash before committing approval.
user_facing_subfeatures: Native Slack, MS Teams, Discord, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Jira, Linear, and ServiceNow channel cards configured via `FEAT-104` Astryx forms. | Stateful PagerDuty / Opsgenie `trigger` + automatic `resolve` correlation on health/breaker recovery. | Interactive Slack & Teams `Approve` / `Reject` cards for `FEAT-068` (Four-Eyes) and `FEAT-078` (`SM-06` MCP HITL) with OIDC step-up safety. | Idempotent Jira / ServiceNow ticket creation for model sunsets (`T-30d`) and high-severity security advisories.
end_to_end_lifecycle: Admin picks connector template (`FEAT-116`) & seals webhook/API token in Vault -> maps severities/categories in Routing Matrix (`FEAT-112`) -> `NOTIFICATION_SINK` formats payload & dispatches via `ARCH-016` -> on recovery event, emits correlated `resolve` payload (or processes verified OIDC-bound `HITL` callback).
primary_and_alternative_journeys:
**Primary (Enterprise Slack + PagerDuty):** `CRITICAL` quorum loss triggers PagerDuty `trigger` + Slack `#sre-incidents`; when DP nodes rejoin (`FEAT-095`), Tanpopo automatically sends PagerDuty `resolve`.
**Alternative (Indie Discord Alerting):** Startup team (`PER-02`) routes model deprecation and budget warnings to a private Discord webhook in 30 seconds.
admin_and_permission_boundaries: Channel configuration requires `ORG_OWNER` / `TEAM_ADMIN` (for project channels) / `OPERATOR`; interactive approvals enforce the exact same RBAC (`SECURITY_REVIEWER` / `ORG_OWNER` + distinct second person for Four-Eyes) as the Web Console — an unmapped chat user is denied `403`.
automation_opportunities: Auto-updating Slack/Teams approval cards in-place (`Approved by @priya at 14:03 UTC`) once resolved via either ChatOps or the Web Console so duplicate clicks are prevented.
enterprise_requirements: Zero unauthenticated chat-ID trust, `SSRFGuard` allowlist enforcement on custom Jira/ServiceNow Enterprise on-prem domains, and full JCS `audit_events` recording (`approval_channel: SLACK_OIDC_VERIFIED`).
touchpoint_console: `/settings/notifications` Connector Gallery & per-connector Astryx setup drawers; `SecurityPage` callback audit trail.
touchpoint_gitops: Declarative `notificationChannels[]` with `${VAULT:...}` secret references.
dependencies_and_relationships: Built on `FEAT-100` (`NOTIFICATION_SINK`), `FEAT-104` (Declarative UI), `FEAT-112` (Routing Matrix), `FEAT-114` (`ARCH-016` Outbox), `FEAT-068` (Four-Eyes), and `FEAT-078` (`SM-06` MCP HITL).

security_privacy_and_financial_implicati: Prevents confused-deputy chat approvals (a compromised Slack guest cannot approve a production policy or MCP tool without passing Tanpopo OIDC/RBAC + Four-Eyes verification).
preliminary_acceptance_criteria: Contract cassette tests verify schema-valid payloads for Slack Block Kit, MS Teams Adaptive Cards, Discord, PagerDuty Events v2 (`trigger` + `resolve` `dedup_key`), Jira, and ServiceNow. | Simulated Slack interactive `Approve` callback with valid Slack HMAC **but** belonging to the original Four-Eyes requester (or an unauthenticated user) is rejected `403` and logged to `audit_events`. | Air-gapped / VPN-only mode degrades gracefully to Console deep-link buttons without requiring public inbound ports.
evidence_and_confidence: `HIGH` — `[SOURCE_VERIFIED]` standard vendor webhook/Events v2 specs and RC9 `SM-06` / `foureyes` primitives (`TEEP-01-DOC-08-05`, `10`).
priority_rationale: P1-Enterprise-Core because enterprise SREs and SecOps teams (`PER-03`, `PER-05`, `PER-08`) live in Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, Jira, and ServiceNow — and should not have to write custom AWS Lambda glue code just to format alerts or approve `SM-06` MCP / Four-Eyes holds safely.
placement_rationale: Ships as signed first-party `NOTIFICATION_SINK` `.tpkg` extensions (`FEAT-100`) running on the hardened async outbox (`ARCH-016`), while Core retains strict OIDC + 5-tuple JCS callback verification for interactive approvals.

name: Turnkey Notification, Observability & Enterprise Integration Setup Templates
target_personas: PER-01;PER-02;PER-03;PER-05;PER-06
plain_language_summary: Eliminates manual URL, port, TLS, and auth-header guesswork by shipping **offline-bundled, step-by-step guided setup wizards** and pre-validated endpoint/payload presets for the most common notification, observability, evaluation, and enterprise security tools — complete with Vault secret sealing and 1-click live test verification.
practical_example: An AI engineer (`PER-02`) wants to export `gen_ai.*` traces to **Langfuse** (self-hosted or cloud) and send alerts to **Telegram**. Instead of reading OTLP/HTTP protobuf path docs or `Base64(pk:sk)` header rules, they click the **Langfuse OTLP** card -> select `EU Cloud` / `US Cloud` / `Self-Hosted URL` -> paste `Public Key` and `Secret Key` (Tanpopo seals both in Vault and formats the exact `Authorization: Basic ...` header + `/api/public/otel/v1/traces` path) -> click `Send Test Span` -> green `Verified (200 OK, 84ms)` in 20 seconds (`[HYPOTHESIS]`).
key_trade_offs: Vendor SaaS endpoints occasionally add new regions or API versions; shipping presets as versioned declarative JSON descriptors (updatable via `.tpbundle` / catalog packs `FEAT-111` and always allowing custom URL override) prevents presets from ever locking users out if a vendor changes a hostname.
user_problem_and_business_value: Bridges the 'last-mile configuration gap' across `DOM-08` (Observability) and `DOM-19` (Notifications): reduces support tickets caused by malformed OTLP paths (`/v1/traces` missing), Gmail SMTP `587 STARTTLS` vs `465 TLS` confusion, or forgotten `--otlp-allowed-cidrs` (`PG-008`) on local Docker collectors.
existing_rc9_behavior_and_limitations: `MISSING` (`[SOURCE_VERIFIED]`): Frozen RC9 requires raw manual URL/JSON entry for webhooks and server-level env vars (`TANPOPO_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, plus undocumented `TANPOPO_OTLP_ALLOWED_CIDRS` `PG-008`) with zero guided integration templates for SMTP providers, Telegram, Slack/Teams, Langfuse, Phoenix, Grafana, Datadog, or Splunk.
proposed_functional_behavior:
Ships an offline-bundled **Integration Template Gallery** (`Settings -> Integrations` & inline drawers in `Observability` / `Notifications`) with Astryx `Stepper` wizards (`1. Choose Region/Mode -> 2. Seal Credentials -> 3. Recommended Events/Sampling -> 4. Live Test Verification`) covering three curated preset families:
1. **Email & Mobile Push Presets (`FEAT-113`):**
   - **Gmail / Google Workspace SMTP** (`smtp.gmail.com:587` `STARTTLS`, App-Password / OAuth guidance).

Detected spans are deterministically replaced per request with typed tokens (<PERSON_01>, <EMAIL_01>, <IBAN_01>, <SSN_01>) stored exclusively in a request-scoped Go map cleared via defer clear(tokenMap). On non-streaming responses, tool-call arguments, and SSE streams (using a bounded prefix-trie lookahead buffer across chunk splits), placeholders are rehydrated prior to client flush.

priority_rationale: During an active zero-day extension compromise, upstream vendor breach, or regulatory directive, a CISO cannot afford to manually log into 15 separate regional/environment Tanpopo instances one by one to trigger quarantines and verify compliance.
